questions.q: What makes the Operations Manager's new request specific enough to build directly?
options: "Late" has an exact definition already available: ShipDate after DueDate, both already pulled in Lesson 3
It requires inventing a new, undefined business rule
It has nothing to do with any data already in the model
It can only be approximated, never calculated exactly
questions.explain: Both ShipDate and DueDate were already in the fact view's source columns, making the late-shipment definition exact and buildable.

questions.q: Why extend the staged view with an IsLate column instead of computing lateness only inside a DAX measure?
options: It follows the established pattern of pushing business rules into the staged view, consistent for every tool that reads it
DAX cannot compare two date columns under any circumstances
Views cannot contain CASE expressions
It has no advantage over a DAX-only approach
questions.explain: Consistent with Lesson 4's approach, pushing the rule into the view keeps the flag available as real data, not just report-layer logic.

questions.q: Why is CREATE OR ALTER VIEW safe to use on the same vw_CarrawayWeeklySalesFact object again?
options: It updates the view in place without breaking the Power BI model's existing relationships to it
It deletes the table and model relationships entirely
It requires rebuilding the entire data model from scratch
It is not safe and should be avoided
questions.explain: Altering the view in place just adds a new column; the existing relationships to Fact remain intact.

questions.q: Why does % Shipped Late use CALCULATE(..., Fact[IsLate] = 1) instead of ALL()?
options: A simple boolean filter respects whatever region/subcategory filters are already active, unlike ALL which would strip them
ALL() is required for every CALCULATE measure
Boolean filters and ALL() behave identically in this context
IsLate cannot be filtered with a boolean condition
questions.explain: A boolean filter argument narrows to late-shipped rows only, while preserving the page's other active filters — unlike ALL, which removes filters.

questions.q: Why did this change request only touch the Drill-Down page, not the Executive Summary page?
options: The Sales Director's requirements were revenue-focused, so adding a fulfillment metric there would be unrequested scope creep
The Executive Summary page cannot technically support new cards
The Operations Manager has no access to the Executive Summary page
Fulfillment data cannot be shown on any executive-level page
questions.explain: Keeping each page scoped to its actual audience avoids growing every page every time any stakeholder asks for something new.
